about: Evidence-graded job-search strategies the local job model learns from (jobmodel.messages). grade: strong (peer-reviewed RCT, meta-analysis or large administrative data), moderate (peer-reviewed with small or unstated effects, or large vendor data with an undisclosed method), weak (surveys, vendor blogs: never given to the model as fact), myth (widely repeated, no source: given to the model as something to correct). Every entry names its source; re-check them when this file changes. Researched 2026-11-18.

strategies.do: Seek a referral or a warm introduction for the roles that matter most: referred applicants are more likely to be hired and stay longer.
strategies.effect: referred hires quit 10-30% less with similar skills (9 firms)
strategies.source: Burks, Cowgill, Hoffman, Housman, Quarterly Journal of Economics 130(2), 2015

strategies.do: Make the resume clear and error-free: better-written applications get hired more often.
strategies.effect: +8% chance of being hired in a randomized field experiment
strategies.source: van Inwegen, Munyikwa, Horton, NBER w30886 / Management Science, 2023-2025

strategies.do: Tailor with specific, checkable facts from the candidate's own record; generic AI-polished wording no longer signals effort.
strategies.effect: employers stop rewarding letters that only look tailored (not yet peer-reviewed)

strategies.do: Adjust how wide the search is: a narrow searcher (few titles, months without offers) should add related occupations; a scattered searcher should narrow.
strategies.effect: suggesting related occupations raised interviews for narrow searchers in a randomized trial
strategies.source: Belot, Kircher, Muller, Review of Economic Studies 86(4), 2019

strategies.do: Apply soon after a posting appears: fewer people apply as it ages, so early applicants face less competition.
strategies.effect: application flow falls with posting age (no effect size published)
strategies.source: Fradkin et al., Management Science (Facebook Jobs data), 2025

strategies.do: Prepare answers in structured-interview form (behavioural STAR stories, situational questions): employers' most predictive interviews are structured.
strategies.effect: structured interview validity .42 vs about .19 unstructured
strategies.source: Sackett et al., Journal of Applied Psychology meta-analysis, 2022

strategies.do: Negotiate a written offer politely with a specific, supported number: negotiators start higher.
strategies.effect: about $5,000 higher starting salary on average (n=149)
strategies.source: Marks and Harold, Journal of Organizational Behavior, 2011

strategies.do: Discount postings that look stale: old, reposted again and again, no named team or pay. Spend effort on fresh, specific ones.
strategies.effect: 18-22% of postings on one large ATS classed as ghost jobs per quarter (method not public)

strategies.do: Do not assume skills-based hiring removes degree or credential screens: state credentials plainly and show skills with evidence.
strategies.effect: only about 3.6% of roles dropped degree requirements; non-degree hires rose about 3.5 points
strategies.source: Burning Glass Institute and Harvard Business School, 2024

strategies.do: Keep a steady daily search effort and act early in a search: callbacks fall the longer someone is out of work, mostly in the first 8 months.
strategies.effect: steep callback decline over the first 8 months of unemployment (resume audit)
strategies.source: Kroft, Lange, Notowidigdo, Quarterly Journal of Economics, 2013

strategies.do: A short thank-you after an interview is courteous.
strategies.effect: HR managers say they consider them (survey, no outcome data)

strategies.do: Exact hours or weekdays to apply.
strategies.effect: vendor blog on a small, likely biased sample

strategies.do: '75% of resumes are auto-rejected by the ATS' is not true: it traces to a resume vendor that published no method. Keyword stuffing and hidden text are seen by recruiters and hurt.
'Referrals are 37x more likely to be hired' and '7% of applicants, 40% of hires' have no published method. Referrals do help (see the QJE study); these numbers are not evidence.
strategies.source: infographics tracing to old vendor marketing
